tasks.short: Coordinate promotions, prepare sales materials and displays, and approve campaign delivery.

steps.what: Agree the promotion objective, audience and constraints with the sales and marketing teams.
Check account segments and recent sales activity in the {CRM}.
Check stock, prices and margins in the {ERP}.
Agree the offer, responsibilities and delivery dates with the marketing team.
Draft advertising copy and display instructions in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Promotion plan, approved claims, brand guidelines and channel templates.
loop.output: Promotion draft and display instructions with claim references.
loop.check: Check prices, dates and required fields against source records; reviewers check claims and tone.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per channel; missing facts or failed checks return to the coordinator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can insert facts, but varied persuasive copy needs language drafting.

steps.what: Arrange the physical demonstration or merchandise display and check its presentation.
Approve the final copy, offer terms and display before customer exposure.
Publish the approved promotion page through the {CMS}.
Schedule the approved campaign send in {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}.
Resolve readiness problems and review early customer responses with the sales team.

tasks.design: Configured views in the {CRM} and {ERP} feed a promotion brief and delivery checklist in {PROJECT}. A template generator in {WORKFLOW} uses a bounded drafting loop for copy in {DOCS}; approved versions flow to the {CMS} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}. Approval binds the exact content, audience and timing, and any change requires renewed approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Offer facts, copy and delivery responsibilities sit in separate systems. Coordination and physical presentation still need people.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval and scheduling features can handle delivery. AI coding reduces the effort of connecting records and templates; bounded drafting can produce a first version.
tasks.still_hard: Persuasive offers, credible claims and team commitments require judgement. Contact permissions, stock changes and physical displays need reliable checks.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor understands customer objections, resolves competing team priorities and judges whether an offer deserves attention.

ambition.what: Weekly promotion continuation, adjustment or withdrawal decisions using response and margin evidence.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less fact gathering and copy assembly, while coordination remains substantial. Within a delegated budget, the supervisor gains a weekly decision on whether to continue, adjust or stop a promotion.

reach.task: Turn a promotion into an account-specific customer conversation.
reach.learn: Learn account segmentation, contact permissions and how to record customer objections.

reach.task: Validate demonstration claims before a promotion is approved.
reach.learn: Learn product limitations, evidence requirements and demonstration readiness.

evidence.claim: Configured reports, templates and approval workflows can reduce promotion preparation and delivery work.
A bounded drafting loop can prepare copy, but factual checks and publication approval remain necessary.
GDPR applies to contact data; national rules determine any employee consultation required by changed processes.

assumptions: The example combines a business-to-business campaign with a showroom or demonstration display; some teams have no physical display.
Shares estimate active task effort across participating roles, excluding waiting time.
The coordination-heavy prior is retained; mailbox work is not assumed to dominate.
Configured publishing and scheduling features are available; custom connectors may be needed.
Build ranges cover one campaign type and include permission checks and any applicable national consultation.
The design uses approved content and campaign data, without employee scoring or profiling.
unknowns: Which promotion channels and physical displays the team actually uses.
Whether stock, price and margin records are current and accessible.
Who can approve offers, claims, audiences and publication.
Whether contact permissions support the intended campaign.
Which national rules and employee consultation arrangements apply.
Whether weekly continuation decisions fall within the supervisor's delegated authority.
research_questions: Can existing systems bind approval to an exact content version, audience and send time?
Which approved claims and channel templates cover the common promotions?
Can campaign responses be linked to sales and margins without adding employee surveillance?
new_work: Review generated copy against approved claims and current offer terms.
Handle stock changes, failed publication and permission exceptions.
Maintain templates, claim references and connector mappings.
Check that approval remains valid when content or audiences change.

tasks.short: Prepare rental or lease agreements with agreed charges, payment terms and signatures.

steps.what: Retrieve customer details and the rental request from the {CRM}.
Check equipment availability and identify the item in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Calculate rental charges, deposits and payment dates in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Resolve requested exceptions to standard charges or lease terms.
Populate the agreement template in {DOCS} with equipment, charges and payment procedures.
Check the completed agreement and approve its release to the customer.
Send the approved agreement for signatures through {ESIGN}.
Review and sign the agreement through {ESIGN}.
File the completed agreement and key dates in the {CLM}.
Enter the agreed billing schedule in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: A configured template in {CLM} fills an agreement from the {CRM}, equipment data in the {OPS_SYSTEM} and a deterministic charge calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. The supervisor approves the exact agreement and recipients before {ESIGN} sends it; completed signatures trigger filing in {CLM} and creation of the billing schedule in the {ERP}. Nonstandard clauses follow the existing approval policy, with no model required.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer details, equipment records, tariffs and document templates are separate. Manual copying provides a workable bridge, while contract exceptions limit full automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Template filling, signature workflows and fixed calculations are established capabilities. AI coding makes the remaining connectors and validation rules cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Availability can change before signature. Nonstandard liability, cancellation or payment terms still require commercial and sometimes legal judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor negotiates workable exceptions and recognises terms that create an unacceptable commercial commitment.

ambition.what: Same-day preparation of standard equipment rental agreements after availability and terms are confirmed.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from copying contract details to resolving exceptions and checking commitments. The supervisor keeps existing signing authority; faster preparation alone grants no new decision rights.

reach.task: Convert signed rental terms into an accurate billing schedule.
reach.learn: Learn deposit treatment, payment dates, equipment identifiers and duplicate prevention.

reach.task: Approve rental terms outside the supervisor's commercial limits.
reach.learn: Learn delegation thresholds, margin implications and liability escalation.

evidence.claim: Structured rental records and approved templates support deterministic agreement preparation.
Signature completion can trigger contract filing and billing data transfer using configured workflows and integrations.
GDPR applies to customer and signatory data; contract and signature requirements depend on the transaction and national rules.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to teams selling equipment rental or lease services.
The typical process uses a tariff workbook and approved document templates; some companies already prepare agreements entirely in the {CLM}.
Shares estimate active effort across participating roles, including customer signature effort but excluding elapsed waiting time.
Standard terms cover most agreements; customer exceptions remain human work.
The supervisor has delegated release authority for standard terms, and any required company signature follows existing policy.
Build ranges cover one agreement family, access review, template validation and applicable national consultation.
No employee monitoring or automated employment decisions are introduced.
unknowns: Which systems hold equipment availability, tariffs and approved templates.
Whether existing template and signature connectors are licensed and available.
Which agreement types and clause exceptions occur most often.
Who has release and signing authority at each commercial threshold.
Whether equipment must be reserved before an agreement is sent.
Which tax, deposit, signature and national contract rules apply.
Whether the finance team requires approval before a billing schedule becomes active.
research_questions: Can existing configuration populate templates without custom document generation?
Which fields and clauses require validation before release?
Can signature completion and billing writes be retried without creating duplicate records?
How should changed availability or expired tariffs invalidate an unissued draft?
new_work: Review agreement exceptions and route terms beyond delegated authority.
Maintain tariffs, approved templates and field mappings.
Resolve failed signatures, stale availability and integration exceptions.
Reconcile signed terms with billing schedules after amendments.
Review access to customer and signatory records.

role.altitude: The supervisor spends less time assembling promotion materials and rental paperwork. Customer judgement, team coordination and commercial exceptions remain central; decision rights expand only where explicitly delegated.
reach: Sales representatives: turn approved promotions into relevant account conversations.
Sales engineers: validate demonstrations and technical claims.
Order clerks: connect signed rental commitments to accurate billing.
Sales managers: decide commercial exceptions beyond local authority.
skills_to_grow: Interpret campaign response and margin evidence.
Write clear briefs and verify customer-facing claims.
Understand rental economics and contract approval limits.
Validate data mappings and recognise failed automation.
Use customer data within established permissions.
role.ambitious_version: Run a weekly promotion decision cycle and offer same-day standard rental agreement preparation, with human approval at customer-facing commitments.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Non-Retail Sales Workers
